original_question: If positive integers a < b have the same radical R(a) = R(b), must there be a prime p with a < p < b?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target statement almost verbatim: it concerns positive integers a<b, assumes equality of radicals R(a)=R(b), and asks whether there must be a prime strictly between a and b.
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, define the operator R(n): for a positive integer n, R(n)=∏_{p|n} p, the radical (squarefree part) of n.
Identify the statement as a conjecture from the paper—specifically Conjecture 2.3, attributed there to Erdős and Dressler.
refined_question: Let R(n)=∏_{p\mid n} p denote the radical (squarefree part) of a positive integer n. If a and b are positive integers with a<b and R(a)=R(b), must there exist a prime number p such that a<p<b?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Conjecture 2.3 in §2.1, not an earlier prime-gap conjecture from §1. Waldschmidt first defines R(n) in §2.1, then discusses related problems about matching prime divisors on intervals (especially Conjecture 2.2), and immediately afterward states Conjecture 2.3 in essentially the same words as your draft. So your draft is already very faithful; the only substantive refinement is to spell out the definition of R(n) and mark the statement as a conjecture.
